headline: High-risk interaction: agentic-flow can execute shell/MCP and modify git, while LlamaFactory is non-interactive and read/write constrained, so most pairwise risks are limited but prompt-injection and cascading-error remain plausible via…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agentic-flow can use MCP, stdin/stdout, and background workers, so if it ingests LlamaFactory outputs through a shared channel, instruction hijacking is plausible. LlamaFactory itself has no filesystem, clipboard, browser, or MCP surface, so the bridge is one-way and indirect. Uncertainty about any shared channel pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agentic-flow consumes LlamaFactory text from stdin/stdout or MCP without provenance filtering, injected instructions can steer tool use.
IF the two agents are connected only by manual copy-paste, the risk remains limited to that bridge.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction parsing on any LlamaFactory-generated text.
Add a fixed delimiter and provenance tag before agentic-flow reads external text.
Review the first 20 lines of any shared prompt before execution.
Route outputs through a human approval step for tool-bearing tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware message filtering.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agentic-flow touches code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, but LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem, clipboard, screen capture, or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel on LlamaFactory, direct leakage from the pair is not evidenced. The main uncertainty is undocumented orchestration, so this stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same shared workspace, agentic-flow could read artifacts that LlamaFactory cannot exfiltrate.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by an external orchestrator that forwards its prompts elsewhere, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in shared prompts or files.
Turn off any automatic prompt logging in the orchestrator.
Inspect outbound destinations for agentic-flow before running sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agentic-flow can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses, while LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no write or shell capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict from LlamaFactory, but agentic-flow's mutable access can still collide with external state if both are pointed at the same repo. Uncertainty about shared targets warrants medium.
conditions: IF agentic-flow and an external wrapper around LlamaFactory target the same git checkout, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF agentic-flow is the only writer, capability conflict is reduced to none.
mitigations: Run agentic-flow on a separate branch.
Serialize any git operations.
Use a lock file around repository mutations.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same checkout.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agentic-flow can produce outputs that downstream systems may treat as authoritative, and its MCP/stdin-stdout surfaces make it easy for LlamaFactory-generated text to become input. LlamaFactory is not runnable and has no verification or action-taking safeguards, so if its text is used as facts, errors can cascade into agentic-flow actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF agentic-flow consumes LlamaFactory output as facts without a verification step, downstream actions may be based on errors.
IF a human reviews every handoff, cascading error risk drops materially.
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before acting on LlamaFactory output.
Mark all LlamaFactory text as untrusted input.
Have agentic-flow cite source lines before taking actions.
Limit autonomous actions to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced in the profiles. agentic-flow lists code, repository metadata, learning patterns, performance metrics, and task prompts, while LlamaFactory lists no data classes touched and no residency, retention, or certification constraints. Without a documented regulated-data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agentic-flow and forwarded to an unapproved service, compliance risk would need reassessment.
IF both agents remain on non-regulated data only, no compliance issue is indicated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document data-class handling before deployment.
Review retention settings in the orchestrator.
Restrict agentic-flow to non-sensitive repositories.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data.
